newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends touch higher after quiet session.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends touch higher after quiet session.

text.p: COMEX copper ended slightly higher after a lackluster session following the expected hike in LME stocks, though much of the rise was metal shuffled from COMEX depots, traders said.
"I think the market right now is generally steady," said Brent Tolen of Triland USA Inc.
LME stocks rose 5,400 tonnes Tuesday to 105,275 tonnes, in line with trader expectations.
Stocks in Long Beach rose and the first batch entered Baltimore. The increase at both locations come from COMEX warehouses, traders said.
LME recently switched to a premium over COMEX in the cash month prompting arbitrage trading to lure metal from COMEX into LME.
March COMEX settled 0.95 cent firmer at 99.55 cents per pound, traded 104.50 to 102.90 cents. Spot December went out 1.35 cents firmer at 104.45 cents.
Volume was estimated at 8,500 lots compared to Monday's official 7,189 lots.
Unlike a fortnight ago, trader worries regarding next week's Third Wednesday pricing on LME have eased.
Looking ahead to the year end and the first quarter, Tolen said the market was set to remain fairly steady.
"I would not fall off my chair if we had a sharp rally, but I would be surprised if we had a sharp selloff," he said.
The copper scrap market was quiet as consumers avoided piling up inventory near year end, said Robert Stein of scrap merchant Louis Padnos Iron & Metal.
"People have their inventory where they want them to be," Stein said.
The export scrap market was also quiet as the Chinese were only looking to buy metal that would be moved in January to arrive after the Chinese New Lunar Year, Stein added.
